correctness.rationale: Exact Fourier orthogonality yields the conditional covariance \(2e^{-s(M+1)}/(1-e^{-s(M+1)})\) for every integer multiplier. Binomial word counts give the finite formula. The uniform geometric denominator error \(O(e^{-s a^n})\), the monotone cost gaps \(F(k+1)-F(k)=s(\rho-1)\rho^k-\tau\), and the suppression factor \(2^n e^{-c a^n}\) establish the staircase. At equality the binomial \(n\)-factor selects the larger minimizer; with \(\tau_n=\tau_j-(\log n-\xi)/a^n\) the exact adjacent ratio tends to \(e^\xi/(j+1)\) while all other modes remain suppressed. All hypotheses, limits, eventual \(\tau_n>0\) and the triangular-array qualification were checked. The 195 checker tests supplement the analytical argument.

originality.rationale: The reviewed originating random beta-map density/response results and broader mixing estimates do not evaluate the specified annealed Poisson-kernel correlations in an exponentially rare horizon-dependent switching regime. Two published exact integer-map results were inspected in full mathematical statements and their proofs: one treats fixed-noise asymptotic variance and one finite rational-grid collapse. Their conclusions do not imply the infinity of dominant rare-word counts or the logarithmically shifted crossover profile. Generic Fourier/binomial/Laplace tools are prior art; novelty is assessed only for the combined sharp natural dynamical phase diagram, with unindexed-equivalence risk retained.
residual_risks: A general mathematical Laplace principle can be specialized to the explicit convex word cost; an equivalent specialized calculation may exist in unindexed literature.
The exact finite Fourier identity is elementary; originality is limited to the combined rare-noise correlation phase staircase and sharp shifted crossover rather than the individual tools.
Broad 2001 analytic toral endomorphism literature was checked through later citations and bibliographic evidence, not all full original texts.

value.rationale: The canonical analytic Poisson observable makes rare-word contributions measurable. General mixing-rate and density theorems do not quantify how an exponentially disappearing probability of the slower map competes with expanding Fourier frequencies. The natural matched scale \(-\log p_n\asymp a^n\) produces an infinite series of phase changes, an exact binomial-multiplicity shift, and a finite-size crossover profile at each boundary. Distinct integer pairs and a precise limitation to triangular arrays support its relevance to singular random expanding dynamics.
